metadata.time_note: Storm Data entry times should be reviewed in local Standard Time (ST), not daylight time. Candidate reports include standard_time_display.
metadata.tornado_track_policy: Tornado tracks must come from DAT. NCEI begin/end coordinates are not used as a tornado track substitute.

properties.event_narrative: Tree down on power lines along North Levisa Road about 1/4 mile away from where it intersects with US-460 ALT. Time estimated to be 14:15z using radar data.
Tree down along S River Road near the intersection with Big Hackneys Creek Road. Time of report estimated to be 14:18z using radar data.
A tree was blown down onto KY 302 near the intersection with Mountain Spring Road. The event time is radar estimated.
A tree was down half way up Sycamore Creek Road_ Van Lear address. The event time is radar estimated.
Downed trees reported on properties along Bullfork Road in Rowan County. Time estimated via radar.

Resends previous tstm wnd dmg report from 3 N Bluestone due to an IRIS error message. Morehead/Rowan County Dispatch received reports of 2 to 3 downed trees in the 800 Block of Sugar Loaf Mountain Road after 6:45 PM. Exact time of report estimated via radar.

Delayed report. Video posted to social media at 7:09 PM on Friday_ 9/4/26 shows large amounts of hail falling into Cave Run Lake and onto boats at Scott Creek Marina. While most of the stones appear to be in the nickel to penny size range_ there are a few larger stones with visible riming and a more elongated structure. The largest stones on the boat were estimated to be around quarter-sized. Time of falling hail estimated to be 7 PM via radar data_ when there was widespread low-level 60-75 dbz reflectivity over this location.

Corrects date of previous tstm wnd dmg report from Mouthcard. Tree down on power lines along North Levisa Road about 1/4 mile away from where it intersects with US-460 ALT. Time estimated to be 14:15z on 9/5/26 using radar data.

Corrects date of previous tstm wnd dmg report from Toonerville. Tree down along S River Road near the intersection with Big Hackneys Creek Road. Time of report estimated to be 14:18z on 9/5/26 using radar data.

Delayed report on social media of sporadic tree damage along Faubush-Norfleet Road from 9/5/26. Pictures show that multiple medium to large trees have large portions broken off of them. There is also fence damage at a property in the 500 Block of the road. The user estimated peak thunderstorm wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph. Time estimated as 6:32 PM using KOHX and KMRX radar data_ as KJKL data was not reporting externally at the time of the event.
Dispatch reported a tree blown down onto and blocking Lloyd Street. Event time estimated from radar.
Dispatch reported a tree blown down onto a home along Rankin Street. No injuries. Time estimated from radar.

During their commute_ an NWS employee observed 4 down trees along US-460 between Murphy Fork Road and Grassy Creek Road. Most of the tree damage was near Mize. One tree was snapped_ another was knocked down into the road. The third was down in a roadside pasture_ and the fourth was down on the hillside/embankment up next to the road. Time estimated as between 12:25 AM and 12:30 AM using radar data.
Trees reported down along Congleton Hollow Rd.
Trees reported down along Pilgrims Rest Rd.
A social media user posted videoes showing rushing water over Ages Creek Road_ as well as reaching the door stoop of a house. Time is estimated based on radar.
Corrects previous flash flood report from Ages. Law enforcement reported KY 38 was shut down at Ages. Pictures showed debris and flowing water over KY-38. Time is estimated.
The public reported KY 38 was shut down at Ages. Pictures showed debris and flowing water over KY-38. Time is estimated.

Rushing water caused damage along Wild Cat Hollow Road_ heading toward the intersection of Kentucky Route 38. Multiple social media posts show both aerial and ground photos of a destroyed fence line_ where large stones and debris were carried down the ditchline before depositing near a residence and the adjacent detached garage building. Rushing water also eroded the property_ leaving a nearby concrete patio undercut.

Social media post from 3:37 PM shows flash flooding on US-119 near the intersection with Intermont Road going up towards Sukey Ridge. Muddy water and debris are visible along the main road_ with deeper water flowing out of the side roads and spilling over onto US-119. There is a car in the ditch further down the hill from where the water was over the road. Commenters state that the driver hydroplaned and lost control.

Social media post from 4:10 PM shows flash flooding along Simpson Lane and Tremont Drive in Harlan County. Muddy_ flowing water has completely covered the road and has washed large tree branches into the middle of the road. Water is beginning to get up on the sides of two shed-type buildings in the pictures.

Video posted to social media at 4:33 pm shows flash flooding along Ages Creek Road in Harlan. The video shows the creek out of its banks and flowing over the road. Water is rapid and muddy. User states that their family is trapped up in Ages Holler due to the road being inundated and impassable. Another social media user in the comments said that water was over the road at the rugby bridge too.

Letcher County Sheriffs Office posted a picture of minor flooding in the Blackey area_ near Frog Pond_ at 4:50 PM. Using Street View imagery_ this was corroborated with a low spot along KY-7 east of Blackey. There are a few inches of standing water on the road_ and it is translucent.
Social media post from 4:56 PM shows water_ mud_ and debris coming off the hillside and blocking both lanes of KY-38 west of Evarts. Location approximated using Street View.

Multiple social media reports between 5:02PM and 5:20 PM demonstrate that flooding caused KY-215 to be completely impassable near the Evarts Church of God. Comments suggest that the road may have been damaged by flood waters. Muddy standing water is visible across both lanes in the later posts. Flowing runoff water likely came off the terrain on the south side of the road as it drained into Yocum Creek at first_ which then inundated the road in the posts. KY-215 was then closed to traffic_ which was redirected.

Picture posted to social media at 5:18 PM shows flowing_ muddy water completely blocking KY0217 in Bell County. Picture taken in an area called Cubbage Hill_ about a mile before the intersection with 217/987. Muddy_ rapidly flowing water is seen spilling out of the ditch and over the road_ with a rapids-type effect visible. The road was impassable.

Delayed report. The Letcher County Sherrifs Office and KSP conducted a water rescue along KY-160 near Kings Creek_ where a vehicle with three occupants became stuck in floodwaters. Time and location estimated using Crest Unit Streamflow data and Streetview imagery.

Multiple videos on Facebook and TikTok show flash flood along Sals Branch in Harlan County. The first video was posted at 5:27 PM. Rapidly flowing muddy water is seen cascading down the road_ which is impassable. Social media posts in the wake of the flood waters indicate that portions of the road were completely washed away. The water line running up the road was exposed to the air due to the water washing away the soils surrounding it. There are large amounts of rock debris visible left behind by the flooding.
Social media report from 5:29pm that minor flooding was ongoing in the lower end of the employee parking lot at the Harlan ARH Hospital.

Social media post from 5:58 PM shows flash flooding in the Brownies Creek/Cubbage Hill area. There is muddy flowing water completely blocking both lanes of KY-217. Comments reveal that the state highway department arrived on scene around 6:30 PM to begin cleanup work.

Social media post from 6:10 PM shows flooding beginning where White Oak Fork dumps into Emily Creek in Pilgrim. Shallow water was beginning to flow over the road_ but the creek remained well in its banks and the bridges were not yet inundated or submerged. A Flood Advisory was issued for this area at 6:04 PM.
At 6:32 PM_ KSP Hazard reported that Highway 160 near Premium was taking on water. The local fire department was dispatched to where a vehicle attempted to drive through the water and got stuck.

At 6:53 PM on 6/23_ NWS RLX received a report of flood waters from Coldwater Fork getting out of its banks and halfway up the sides of vehicles parked between Megan Lane and Parsons Branch in Martin County KY.

At 6:58 PM_ KSP Harlan reported that multiple bridges were washed out in hollers in the community of Ages in Harlan County. KSP passed along that road crews were headed to the scene to assess the situation further.

Social media post from 7PM shows extensive post-flood debris blocking KY-588 in the UZ community. Poster states_ quote: So many places had so much water it was dangerous. The water is also all the way across the road on 588 going towards 160. End quote. As of 3 AM on 9/24/26_ KY-588 is marked as closed between Hancock Drive and Cr-1713. It is likely that the peak of the flash flooding was before the time of the social media post_ but this incident left lasting impacts.

Social media user reported that the flash flooding at the intersection of White Oak Fork and Emily Creek was worsening. They were evacuating their family and their horses to a safer place/higher ground due to the rising water. This corresponds with a robust 200-600+ cfs MRMS Crest Unit Streamflow signal in E Martin County.
In the past 8 hours or so.

Social media report of flash flooding in the Wallins Creek and South Wallins communities of Harlan County. The video shows water flowing over KY-219 between the post office and the Baptist Church. The user states that the water was deeper on the back road (South Wallins Avenue) behind the post office building. That road is closer to Wallins Creek. Poster states that the video was taken at 9:22 PM.

Social media report from 9:40 PM depicts flash flooding along Terry Fork in the Wallins Creek community. Flowing water came out of the banks and covered the intersection of Grammar Lane and Sycamore Drive. Water was inundating the garage of a residence in this area. Debris was reportedly accumulating atop a nearby bridge as the flood waters continued.

A delayed social media post shows Ewing Creek rushing over Ewing Creek Rd near Williams Drive in the Dayhoit community. Additional photographs show damage to the street_ with displaced pieces of pavement along the road. Time estimated using peak Crest Unit Streamflow signal.

Social media post from 10:06 PM on 9/23 depicts flash flooding along Pine Branch Road in Grays Knob. Video shows muddy_ rushing water rapidly flowing down the hill and completely covering the roadway. Individual states that there is no way in our out of the road due to the raging water. There are reports of a potential landslide along the road as well.

Social media posts from the Yancey_ Gulston_ and Pansy communities reveal flash flooding in southern Harlan County during the late evening hours on 9/23. The first post was from 10:43 PM_ asking for help from neighbors as water rose. Pictures after sunrise on 9/24 reveal that water from the flash flooding got into the utility room of a home along Slaters Fork Road southeast of Pansy. Pictures show debris and mud left behind in the yard_ damaged fencing_ and a displaced/damaged wooden playhouse. Additional posts discuss flooding along the back lane in Pansy_ but with limited details.

Social media report of the Bobs Creek Tunnel being totally inundated by flood waters during the evening round of flash flooding on 9/23. Pictures from after dawn on 9/24 reveal that there is still standing water in the tunnel_ but there is also multiple logs and debris making the tunnel impassable. It appears that there was at least 3 feet of water in the tunnel based on the water/mud marks visible on the walls of the tunnel. Time estimated using peak Crest Unit Streamflow data. There were 5 pixels of 1000+ cfs upstream of this location along KY-1556. That area drains towards this tunnel.

Delayed social media posts from the Pansy area of Harlan County reveal that flash flooding during the late evening hours on 9/23. These posts came after dawn on 9/24. The Pansy Missionary Baptist Church posted that the flood waters made it into their basement. Additional pictures show large tree debris_ basketball goals_ and blue pipes washed into the yards of residents living along Pansy Loop. One individual reported that their fence was completely swept away by the floodwaters. Time estimated using crest unit streamflow.

Social media post from 10:55 PM on 9/23 shows flash flooding in a holler off of KY-2425 in the Teeterville/Catron Creek part of Harlan County. Videos depict raging muddy water coming down the hillside and completely covering the road. The poster states that they had to use a truck to pull the trailers of two family members out of the rising water. Additional pictures show trees that have been downed by the floodwaters and carried down the hill.
